findings.description: PyYAML `UnsafeConstructor.find_python_module` calls `__import__(name)` on a fully attacker-controlled module name taken from the YAML `!!python/module:<name>` tag, enabling arbitrary module import / gadget loading when the unsafe loader is used
findings.reasoning: `construct_python_module()` (registered as a multi-constructor for the `tag:yaml.org,2002:python/module:` prefix) takes the tag suffix straight from the YAML document and passes it to `find_python_module()`. When invoked through `UnsafeConstructor` (i.e. `yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.Loader)` / `yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.UnsafeLoader)` / `yaml.unsafe_load`), `unsafe=True` and the attacker-controlled string reaches `__import__(name)` — a direct code-execution/deserialization sink, since importing an arbitrary module can trigger module-level side effects, and the returned module object is then available to be combined with the `python/object`, `python/object/apply` and `python/name` constructors that follow to reach arbitrary callables. No validation, allow-list or sandboxing of the module name occurs. This is a genuine dangerous-deserialization sink of the library (documented as unsafe, but still a live attack surface for every consumer that passes untrusted YAML to the `Loader`/`UnsafeLoader` API, which was the default `yaml.load` behaviour for the entire 3.x/4.x/5.0 line).

evidence.dataflow_analysis: YAML tag suffix (attacker controlled) -> construct_python_module(suffix, node) -> find_python_module(suffix, node.start_mark) -> UnsafeConstructor.find_python_module(..., unsafe=True) -> __import__(name)
evidence.notes: Version string is 5.3; `Loader`/`UnsafeLoader`/`unsafe_load` all route to UnsafeConstructor -> Constructor(UnsafeConstructor). lib/yaml/constructor.py (py2 tree) has the identical sink at line 520.

findings.description: PyYAML `UnsafeConstructor.find_python_name` calls `__import__(module_name)` on the attacker-controlled dotted name from `!!python/name:` / `!!python/object:` tags, enabling import of arbitrary modules before resolving arbitrary attributes via getattr
findings.reasoning: The tag suffix of `!!python/name:<mod>.<attr>` / `!!python/object:<mod>.<cls>` is split into module and object name and, under `UnsafeConstructor` (unsafe=True), the module part is passed to `__import__()`. The resolver then does `getattr(module, object_name)` and the result is used by `make_python_instance()` to run `cls(*args, **kwds)`. This gives an attacker a two-stage primitive: import an arbitrary module (arbitrary code executed at import time) and obtain a reference to any attribute/callable in it, which is exactly the classic unsafe-YAML RCE chain (`!!python/object/apply:os.system ["id"]`). No allow-list or validation is applied to the name.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: YAML tag suffix -> construct_python_name / construct_python_object / construct_python_object_apply -> find_python_name(suffix, node.start_mark) -> UnsafeConstructor.find_python_name(..., unsafe=True) -> __import__(module_name) -> sys.modules[module_name] -> getattr(module, object_name) -> make_python_instance -> cls(*args)
evidence.notes: Identical sink in the py2 tree at lib/yaml/constructor.py:540 (unsafe=True). Reachable via yaml.Loader/UnsafeLoader/unsafe_load and via yaml.load(..., Loader=Loader).

findings.description: Python 2 (lib/) FullConstructor.find_python_module performs __import__(name) on an attacker-controlled module name taken from a YAML tag suffix, enabling arbitrary module import / code execution via yaml.load
findings.reasoning: In the Python 2 tree (lib/), `FullConstructor.find_python_module()` accepts a `name` that comes straight from the multi-constructor suffix of a `!!python/module:<name>` tag (see `construct_python_module()`, which passes the tag suffix to `find_python_module(suffix, node.start_mark)`). When called through `UnsafeConstructor.find_python_module()` (line 716-717) `unsafe=True`, the attacker-controlled string is passed directly to the builtin `__import__()`. Loading an untrusted document with the default `yaml.load()` (which maps to `Loader` -> `Constructor` -> `UnsafeConstructor` in this version) therefore gives an attacker the ability to import arbitrary modules, and combined with `!!python/object/apply:` / `!!python/object/new:` this leads to full remote code execution. This is a classic insecure deserialization sink (CWE-502/CWE-94) in the library core, not test or build code.

evidence.code_context: lib/yaml/constructor.py:514-527 find_python_module().__import__(name) inside `if unsafe:`; lib/yaml/constructor.py:556-560 construct_python_module() -> self.find_python_module(suffix, node.start_mark); lib/yaml/constructor.py:715-717 UnsafeConstructor.find_python_module(name, mark) -> super(...).find_python_module(name, mark, unsafe=True); lib/yaml/loader.py Loader = Reader/Scanner/.../Constructor, and lib/yaml/constructor.py:720 class Constructor(UnsafeConstructor)

evidence.notes: Two sink variants per tree: module import (this one) and name lookup/instantiation (find_python_name/make_python_instance) which additionally call getattr(cls) and cls(*args, **kwds) allowing arbitrary callables (e.g. os.system, subprocess.Popen).

findings.description: Python 2 (lib/) FullConstructor.find_python_name performs __import__(module_name) plus getattr() on attacker-controlled names from YAML tag suffixes, allowing arbitrary code execution via yaml.load
findings.reasoning: `find_python_name()` takes the suffix of `!!python/name:`, `!!python/object:`, `!!python/object/new:` and `!!python/object/apply:` tags (attacker controlled) and splits it into module/object. With `unsafe=True` (UnsafeConstructor path used by the default `Loader`/`Constructor` in this tree), it calls `__import__(module_name)` and then `getattr(module, object_name)`, returning an arbitrary callable. That callable is then invoked by `make_python_instance()` (`cls(*args, **kwds)` / `cls.__new__(cls, *args, **kwds)`) with attacker supplied args/kwds, and `set_python_instance_state()` calls `__setstate__` or `setattr` on the instance. Result: arbitrary code execution from untrusted YAML (CWE-502/CWE-94). This is real library code (not a test/build artifact).

evidence.code_context: lib/yaml/constructor.py:529-545 find_python_name(): __import__(module_name) and getattr(module, object_name); lib/yaml/constructor.py:571-590 make_python_instance() -> cls(*args, **kwds) / cls.__new__(cls,*args,**kwds); lib/yaml/constructor.py:592-605 set_python_instance_state() -> instance.__setstate__(state) / setattr(instance, key, value); lib/yaml/constructor.py:718-720 UnsafeConstructor.find_python_name(...,unsafe=True); lib/yaml/constructor.py:723 class Constructor(UnsafeConstructor)
evidence.dataflow_analysis: YAML tag suffix (e.g. 'os.system') -> construct_python_object_apply/construct_python_object -> make_python_instance(suffix,...) -> find_python_name(suffix, mark, unsafe=True) -> __import__ + getattr -> cls(*args, **kwds) => arbitrary function invocation
evidence.notes: Registered multi-constructors for python/name:, python/module:, python/object:, python/object/new: and UnsafeConstructor python/object/apply: all funnel into these two sinks.

findings.description: yaml.load() defaults to FullLoader (PyYAML 5.3), which still constructs !!python/object/new instances, allowing arbitrary code execution from untrusted YAML (CVE-2020-1747)
findings.reasoning: `yaml.load()` without an explicit Loader falls back to `FullLoader`. In this 5.3 version FullConstructor registers multi-constructors for `tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object:`, `python/object/new:` and `python/name:` (constructor.py:699-713). `make_python_instance` only requires a `type` when `unsafe` is False, so `!!python/object/new:subprocess.Popen` / `!!python/object/new:os.system` style payloads reach `cls.__new__(cls, *args, **kwds)` and execute attacker-controlled callables, and `set_python_instance_state` calls `__setstate__`/`update`/`setattr` which yields further gadget chains (e.g. `!!python/object/new:type` + `!!python/name:eval`). This is exactly CVE-2020-1747 - FullLoader was not safe for untrusted input; the safe default (`SafeLoader`) is only used in `safe_load`. Any application calling `yaml.load(user_input)` or `yaml.load(request.data)` gets RCE.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: stream (attacker YAML) -> FullLoader -> FullConstructor.construct_yaml_object/construct_python_object_apply -> make_python_instance -> cls(*args, **kwds) / cls.__new__(cls, *args, **kwds); also set_python_instance_state -> instance.__setstate__(state)
evidence.notes: PyYAML version 5.3 (lib/yaml/__init__.py:11 -> __version__ = '5.3'). FullLoader is documented as 'Resolve all tags except those known to be unsafe', but CVE-2020-1747 showed python/object/new via FullLoader still gives RCE; fixed in 5.4 by restricting FullConstructor.

findings.description: yaml.full_load()/full_load_all() explicitly use FullLoader, enabling python/object/new object construction and code execution on untrusted input
findings.reasoning: `full_load`/`full_load_all` are public top-level APIs that intentionally use `FullLoader`. In 5.3 the FullConstructor still registers `python/object:`, `python/object/new:` and `python/name:` multi-constructors and `make_python_instance` invokes `cls.__new__(cls, *args, **kwds)` for any class (only non-class callables are blocked when unsafe=False). The docstring's claim that the resolved tags are not "unsafe on untrusted input" is therefore false for this version (CVE-2020-1747). Applications that follow the API naming and call `full_load()` on user input are exploitable.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: attacker stream -> load(stream, FullLoader) -> FullConstructor.add_multi_constructor('tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/new:') -> construct_python_object_new -> construct_python_object_apply -> make_python_instance -> cls.__new__(cls, *args, **kwds)
evidence.notes: __init__.py lines 142 and 152 are the FullLoader uses flagged; both reachable from public API.

findings.description: FullConstructor (used by FullLoader, the default for yaml.load in 5.3) registers the python/object: multi-constructor, allowing arbitrary object instantiation from untrusted YAML (CVE-2020-1747 class)
findings.reasoning: In this tree (version 5.3), FullConstructor and not only UnsafeConstructor registers the `!!python/object:` / `!!python/object/new:` multi-constructors. construct_python_object() -> make_python_instance() calls `cls(*args, **kwds)` (or `cls.__new__`) for any class reachable through find_python_name(), and construct_python_object_apply() then applies state/listitems/dictitems. Because yaml.load() defaults to FullLoader (FullConstructor) and full_load()/full_load_all() explicitly use it, simply parsing an attacker-supplied YAML document can instantiate arbitrary classes and invoke `__setstate__`/`__init__` logic, giving code execution. This is exactly CVE-2020-1747, fixed in 5.3.1 by removing these constructors from FullConstructor. Severity high: document parsing of untrusted input is common and requires no extra preconditions.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: yaml.load(stream) (Loader=None) -> Loader = FullLoader -> get_single_data() -> construct_object with tag 'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object:...' -> construct_python_object -> make_python_instance -> cls(*args, **kwds) => arbitrary callable invocation
evidence.notes: version 5.3 in lib3/yaml/__init__.py:11 confirms the CVE-2020-1747 window (fixed in 5.3.1).

findings.description: FullConstructor registers python/object: multi-constructor in the Python 2 tree, enabling arbitrary object instantiation from untrusted YAML (CVE-2020-1747 class)
findings.reasoning: Same defect in the Python 2 source tree: FullConstructor (the class behind FullLoader, used by yaml.load default and full_load/full_load_all) registers python/object:, python/object/new:, python/name: and python/module:. Attacker-controlled YAML parsed by an application using yaml.load() can therefore resolve arbitrary dotted names via find_python_name() and instantiate them (make_python_instance -> cls(*args, **kwds)), plus apply state via set_python_instance_state, resulting in arbitrary code execution. Version 5.3 predates the 5.3.1 fix for CVE-2020-1747.

findings.description: yaml.load() with no Loader silently defaults to FullLoader, which in 5.3 still permits full constructor (python/object) construction — unsafe default deserialization
findings.reasoning: The top-level API used by virtually every consumer of PyYAML (yaml.load()) picks FullLoader, and in this 5.3 tree FullConstructor registers python/object, python/object/new, python/name and python/module (only python/object/apply is restricted to UnsafeConstructor). A warning is emitted but parsing proceeds, so any application that calls yaml.load(untrusted_string) — the historical idiomatic usage preserved for backwards compatibility — is exploitable for object instantiation/code execution. That is CVE-2020-1747 (fixed in 5.3.1 by further restricting FullLoader).

evidence.code_context: if Loader is None: load_warning('load'); Loader = FullLoader; loader = Loader(stream); return loader.get_single_data()
evidence.dataflow_analysis: user YAML string -> yaml.load -> FullLoader -> FullConstructor.construct_python_object/new -> make_python_instance -> arbitrary callable
evidence.notes: Same pattern repeated in load_all (line 125), full_load (142), full_load_all (152).

findings.description: yaml.load()/load_all() default to FullLoader in the Python 2 tree, which permits python/object construction of untrusted YAML
findings.reasoning: Same unsafe default in lib/yaml/__init__.py: with Loader=None, yaml.load() (and yaml.load_all at line ~130, plus full_load/full_load_all at 147/157) uses FullLoader. FullConstructor in this 5.3 tree registers the python/object and python/object/new multi-constructors, so untrusted YAML such as `!!python/object/new:os.system ["id"]` executes code during parsing. Being a library default, every downstream caller inheriting it is vulnerable (CVE-2020-1747).

findings.description: FullConstructor registers python/name: and python/module: multi-constructors, letting untrusted YAML resolve arbitrary dotted Python names/modules under FullLoader
findings.code_snippet:
FullConstructor.add_multi_constructor(
    u'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/name:',
    FullConstructor.construct_python_name)

FullConstructor.add_multi_constructor(
    u'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/module:',
    FullConstructor.construct_python_module)
findings.reasoning: find_python_name() resolves any already-imported module attribute (getattr(sys.modules[module_name], object_name)) and find_python_module() returns the module object; both are reachable from FullConstructor, i.e. from the default FullLoader. The resulting objects are then used by construct_python_object_apply/new as the callable to instantiate, so an attacker can chain `!!python/name:` to obtain an arbitrary callable and invoke it with attacker args. This provides gadget availability even when the explicit python/object tag path is restricted, and is part of the CVE-2020-1747 attack surface.

evidence.code_context: construct_python_name -> find_python_name(suffix) -> getattr(sys.modules[module_name], object_name); then make_python_instance calls cls(*args, **kwds)
evidence.dataflow_analysis: YAML tag suffix (attacker controlled) -> find_python_name/find_python_module -> getattr on imported module -> used as callable in construct_python_object_apply
